title: Rechargeable free tier with staged upgrade prompts to increase PLG conversion
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal:
Run a controlled experiment to validate whether a 'rechargeable' free tier (periodic re-crediting) + staged upgrade prompts improves PLG conversion and long-term engagement without increasing support load or abuse. This builds on prior credit/expiry experiments but focuses on cadence and prompt placement rather than raw credit size.

Background:
- We continue to see drop-off when trial credits expire; previous trials (PM-5512, PM-7439) varied size and expiry. Feedback indicates users abandon before re-evaluating upgrade.
- Hypothesis: periodic small re-credits (e.g., monthly micro-topups) combined with contextual, staged upgrade prompts (in-editor, quota-burn warning, and after high-value action) will nudge conversion and reduce churn.

Experiment design (variants):
- Control: existing 14-day credit + one-time expiry email reminder (status quo).
- Variant A (Cadence): Rechargeable free tier: initial credit (50k tokens), then monthly micro-credit top-ups of 5k tokens for 3 months unless user upgrades. Expiry on each top-up = 30 days.
- Variant B (Prompting): Status quo credits but with staged in-product upgrade prompts placed at 3 trigger points: (1) 80% of initial credit used, (2) after 2 high-value generation events, (3) at end of 14-day window. Prompts include a time-limited discount CTA.
- Variant C (Combo): Rechargeable top-ups + staged prompts.

Success metrics and measurement:
- Primary metric: 30-day PLG upgrade rate (proportion of users upgrading to paid within 30 days).
- Secondary metrics: 60-day retention of trial users, support ticket rate per experiment cohort, fraud/abuse signals (account creation velocity, IP anomalies), Net MRR uplift per cohort.
- Monitor token consumption distribution, session frequency, and latency to first paid conversion.

Rollout plan and instrumentation:
- A/B randomization by account id at sign-up. Split traffic evenly across control + 3 variants. Target minimum detectable effect: +12% relative improvement in 30-day upgrade rate with 80% power.
- Event schema: capture 'credit_granted', 'credit_expired', 'upgrade_prompt_shown', 'upgrade_click', 'account_upgraded', 'support_ticket_created'. Product analytics (Amplitude) dashboards will be pre-built.
- Tracking responsibility: ENG-2174 (billing events pipeline), DES-342 (prompt creative and variations).

Trade-offs and risks:
- Abuse: rechargeable credits may be exploited by bad actors. Mitigation: rate-limit top-ups per IP/account fingerprint; require minimal verification after 2 months for repeated free usage. Telemetry flagged to security team.
- Cost: incremental compute/embedding cost from extended free usage; finance to run ROI sensitivity (acceptable within experimentation budget).
- Friction: too frequent prompts may annoy users; staged prompt cadence must be validated with qualitative feedback.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Product: finalize variant copy, CTA offers, and success guardrails. (owner: Asha)
- Design: create prompt mockups, empty-state flows, and microcopy testing (owner: Priya Rao).
- Engineering: backend credit top-up logic, billing telemetry, AB test flags, rollback hooks (owners: Diego Alvarez, ENG-2174).
- Analytics: pre-register metrics and dashboards, QA instrumentation (owner: Marco Chen).
- Legal/Security: review TOS/anti-abuse policy updates if needed (owner: Legal).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Experiment is instrumented with deterministic cohort assignment and events emitted for all key actions.
2) No more than 2% increase in support tickets in any variant for the first 7 days (if exceeded, pause variant).
3) Fraud signals do not materially increase (security sign-off).
4) Dashboards show cohort-level primary/secondary metrics within 48 hours of rollout.
5) UX flows approved by design and copy signed off by PM.

Known links and artifacts:
- Experiment PRD (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/PLG+Rechargeable+Free+Tier
- Figma prompt mocks: https://www.figma.com/file/example/rechargeable-prompts
- GH: feature branch and server-side flags: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8721
- Analytics spec: https://amplitude.com/redwood/experiment-7981/spec

Next steps:
- 02/12: Finalize copy and offer tiers (PM + Design).
- 02/16: ENG provide ETA for pipeline work and gating checklist.
- 02/20: Analytics QA and security review.
- 02/25: Target experiment launch to 10% traffic; scale if metrics stable.

Notes on employer contract/security questionnaire impact:
- This experiment does not change enterprise contract terms. For customers on Dedicated/Private who are eligible for special credits in contract, the rechargeable free tier will be disabled. Flagging required: release notes + sales playbook updates.
